prompt:
Style: notebook-hand-drawn. Transform the supplied ORIGINAL photograph of a LEGO Millennium Falcon model on a white cabinet, minifigures, a display plaque and nearby autumn foliage. Render only a single full-frame artwork using this style treatment:

The artwork is a complete reinterpretation: 100% illustration, 0% photography, in a delicate botanical-ink style drawn with a fine black fineliner and controlled parallel and cross-hatching. It first picks out the photo's most recognizable subjects and relationships, keeps their defining features in restrained linework, and removes clutter — some areas intricate, others minimal or entirely blank for deliberate negative space. Color is strictly rationed: two dominant colors extracted from the photo plus one derived complementary accent, black ink, and warm-white paper — nothing else. The color goes on as large, flat, irregular abstract blocks (broad-marker organic shapes) laid behind and around the subject as an independent layer; blocks may cross the ink lines or disappear behind the subject, with intentional imperfections and a few small dots for rhythm, like a handmade screen-print or sketchbook page. The background is dramatically simplified — a few essential contours plus generous warm-white negative space — on heavyweight warm-white notebook paper with subtle fibers and grain. Explicitly excluded: photorealism, digital-painting and 3D looks, smooth gradients, watercolor bleeding, colored outlines, busy backgrounds, full-coverage coloring, perfect geometry, generic floral decoration, arbitrary colors, and dense all-over linework. 

Preserve the original scene's subject relationships. Every part of the canvas must belong to the transformed artwork. No original photo panel, no before/after comparison, no split, no text.
